did_you_know.text: Did you know? This chapter describes how Satan incited David to take a census of Israel, even though the census was not presented here as a military or administrative necessity.
Did you know? Joab objected to the census order and warned David that it could bring guilt upon Israel, but he ultimately carried out the king’s command.
Did you know? According to the numbers Joab reported, Israel had 1,100,000 men who could wield a sword, and Judah had 470,000.
Did you know? Levi and Benjamin were not included in the census; according to the text, Joab did not complete it because the king’s command was detestable to him.
Did you know? After realizing the seriousness of his actions, David openly confessed, “I have sinned greatly,” and asked the Lord to take away his guilt.
Did you know? The prophet Gad presented David with three possible punishments: three years of famine, three months of fleeing from his enemies, or three days of plague in the land.

Did you know? David chose to fall into the hands of the Lord rather than into human hands because he said that the Lord’s mercies are great; in this way, he chose the punishment that was subject to God’s mercy.
Did you know? David and the elders saw the angel of the Lord standing between earth and heaven with a drawn sword stretched out over Jerusalem, and they fell facedown while clothed in sackcloth.

Did you know? When Ornan offered to give David the threshing floor and everything needed for the sacrifice, David refused, saying that he would not offer the Lord a burnt offering that cost him nothing.
Did you know? After David built an altar and offered sacrifices on it, the Lord answered him with fire from heaven; afterward, the angel put his sword back into its sheath.
